# Context Compression Pipeline Maintenance

## When to use
- Auditing a context/token compression pipeline for correctness or efficiency.
- Investigating why compression is defeated (reverted_gate, 0-saving, over-broad detection).
- Applying a surgical fix to polarity, slot normalization, hashing, or storage.

## Procedure (in order)
1. Read the actual source (detection, core compression, storage) — do not guess.
2. Form a hypothesis; run an empirical test BEFORE editing to confirm the bug exists.
3. Apply the smallest surgical fix at the root cause in shared code (not at call sites).
4. Re-run the empirical test to confirm the fix; run the full test suite.
5. Re-run latency benchmarks 2-3x to rule out scheduler noise.

## Always-on rules
- Never loosen fail-open: compression must never raise or block the original output.
- Detection polarity must be precise. Loose substring matching (e.g., "error" in "no error") locks benign lines and defeats compression. Use word boundaries + negation handling; real error signals on the same line must survive.
- Keep the expensive detection regex behind a prefilter that is a *strict superset* of it. `is_important` → `_compute_fault` → `looks_suspicious` → one 614-char case-insensitive `_ERROR_RE`. Loose hints ("status", "sig", "memory", "http") let every info log line reach that alternation at ~42µs/line: 1.3s on a 20K-line dump, which then exceeds the fail-open guard and pays nothing. Assert the literal prefix first instead (`_STATUS5_RE`, `_HTTP5_RE`, `_HEX_FRAME_RE`) and prove the superset property by differential test, not by inspection: over ~89K real lines, zero lines may be rejected by the prefilter that the precise regex would match. Fixing this beat every other optimisation available (1206ms → 118ms on 20K lines) and is the concrete reason not to port the compressor to a faster language.
- Profile before blaming the interpreter. `_classify` (one `is_important` per line) is the compressor's dominant cost, not token estimation (`estimate_tokens` 1.8ms vs `_classify` 1206ms on the same 20K-line payload) and not `strip_ansi` (0.4ms). Rewriting in Rust would have preserved the pathological regex at 10x the cost.
- Slot normalization must not collapse distinct values that carry meaning (ports, config values).
- Content-addressed storage keys must be collision-resistant (full hash, not truncated).
- Never emit retrieval markers that cannot be resolved (e.g., in-memory-only aliases). When SQLite write or commit fails in CCR, return "" (fail open) rather than inventing an in-memory alias that dies with the process.
- CCR retrieval alias fastpath: never call legacy filesystem globbing (`_file_get`) on `#c...` Base62 aliases. When `default_dir()` (`~/.trimtok`) exists on disk, checking filesystem `.txt` files before SQLite strips `#c1` to `c1` and globs `c1*.txt`, causing catastrophic cache collisions with old files. Always query `FastCCRStore` (RAM LRU -> SQLite WAL) directly for `#c...` aliases.
- Atomic cross-process alias allocation: never cache an alias sequence counter in Python RAM across calls — parallel subagents sharing the CCR database will read stale values and collide on #cN aliases. Always allocate sequence numbers atomically in SQLite (`INSERT INTO meta ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`).
- Move storage imports (ccr) to module level — importing inside the hot path bills the one-time module load on every call (~700ms). Profile latency 2-3x after every change; a regression that persists (not just noise) is real.
- README reduction numbers must cite real telemetry (usage.jsonl) and be computed from `saved` (see Measurement polarity). Label synthetic cases as "ceiling reference only." When the README number and a fresh honest audit disagree, the README is wrong — correct it in the same pass; an inflated claim in the repo is a lie the next session will optimise against.
- Before adding a new dependency, check if an existing dep is underutilized (rapidfuzz was already a dep but only used in delta_engine). Reject deps > 20MB or with model weights. Zero-model, deterministic philosophy must be preserved.
- Version sync: VERSION in core.py, pyproject.toml, and plugin.yaml must all match. Bump all three together on every release. A mismatch (e.g., 4.2.2 vs 4.2.3) confuses consumers and breaks plugin loaders that read plugin.yaml.
- Cleanup: when the user says "verify from real usage only," remove synthetic test files (stress_heavy.py, benchmark_v42.py) and old review/plan reports (reports/) that inflate or misrepresent numbers. Keep real regression tests (test_core, test_dedup, etc.) as guards. Remove dead shims (ccr_v2, root-level one-liners) only after confirming no test imports them. Run all tests after cleanup.
- Run tests after every change. A latency regression that disappears on re-run is noise, not a real regression.

## Telemetry hygiene (do this before any optimisation claim)
- Cross-check every distinct `gate` and `kind` value in the log against the source tree. A value that exists only under `tests/` (mocked stats dicts) is test traffic that leaked into production usage.jsonl; fixture-shaped commands in the log confirm it. Exclude test-only gates from every aggregate and make tests point the data-home env var at a temp dir — polluted telemetry invalidates exactly the before/after comparison you need to prove an improvement.
- Bind each gate to one cause, or record a `reason`. One gate name covering four return sites (file below min_chars, targeted slice, anti-poisoning rail, cold-read fallback) makes a deliberate rule indistinguishable from a dead branch, and you will guess for an hour. Add a one-word `reason` to any gate with more than one return site before drawing conclusions from counts.
- A retrieve counter is not evidence of retrieval value: count DISTINCT refs and their inter-arrival gaps. Thousands of `hook=retrieve` rows collapsing to a handful of distinct hashes with a ~0s median gap is a test loop hammering one alias, not agent behaviour. Real agents resolve under ~1% of emitted #refs, so fold-induced information loss is invisible in the retrieve log — judge folds by whether the agent re-reads or repairs afterwards, never by retrieve hit rate.
- Latency guard must clear the real p99 with margin. A 50ms guard against a measured p99 of 63ms / max 145ms dumps whole payloads into passthrough_timeout and quietly costs ~2% of all tokens; 150-250ms is imperceptible inside a tool call and buys that traffic back.

## Audit order (token value, not event count)
1. Honest metric + metric self-check (above). Without it every later decision is measuring the wrong thing.
2. Zero-bucket inventory: sum `before` tokens per gate, sorted descending. The largest bucket with 0% saving is the work item — a name that says "passthrough_small" may still be carrying 8% of all tokens.
3. Anything the pipeline is CAPABLE of but never does in production: reproduce it in-process (import the compressor, feed a real payload of the real shape) before touching a threshold. A capability that scores 60% in-process and 0% in the log is a routing bug or a rule that excludes the median input — not a ratio problem.
4. Reverts and timeouts: audit whether the guard is correct or merely paranoid, and whether the guard budget is the binding constraint, before widening anything.
5. Only then structural passes, chosen by token weight of the biggest `shape`, never by the most frequent event type. Event count and token weight diverge hard: most events save <50 tokens each (~1% of savings) while a small minority of long outputs carries ~92%. Optimise top-N long outputs and report concentration plus peak context, not the mean.

## Verification
- Empirical: build a benign log containing fault-keywords ("no error", "error-handling") and assert gate == ok and saved > 0.
- Regression: real errors (Traceback, RuntimeError, FAILED, ERROR:, HTTP 5xx, exit code, panic, assert) still detected; benign URLs ignored.
- Suite: run all test_*.py; benchmark 2-3x to rule out scheduler noise.
- Latency: calibrate with a 20,000-line unique-line payload (the shape that exposes superlinear detection cost), not with 500-line samples. As of 4.2.6: `_classify` 118ms, full `compress_terminal` on 1.56MB ≈ 163ms, which fits inside the 200ms guard.
- Retrieval: for every digest-based #ref a compressor emits, assert compress → retrieve(hash=digest) == original (end-to-end). A marker that cannot resolve is a bug, not a feature.
- Measurement polarity (the metric that has burned this project): compute reduction from the per-event `saved` field only — `sum(saved)/sum(before)`. NEVER `1 - sum(after)/sum(before)`: `after` is written only for rows that were actually rewritten, so every passthrough row contributes `after=0` and the formula silently scores "nothing happened" as 100% saved. On real trimtok telemetry the buggy formula reported 49.0% terminal / 43.8% tool while the honest number was 13.7% / 7.0% — a 3.5x overclaim that reached the README and the skill itself. Self-check on every audit: for `gate=ok` rows assert `saved ≈ before - after`; a mismatch means the fields disagree and no aggregate built on them is trustworthy.
4.2.6 implemented the rules above: `after == before` on passthrough rows, a `reason` per gate, `guard_ms` 200, `shape="ref-verbatim"` for the read_file band, test doubles with `usage_enabled: False` (mocked `gate="small"` rows purged from usage.jsonl), and the literal-prefix prefilter. Honest post-purge baseline: 4,323 events, 13.7% terminal / 7.5% tool / 9.5% overall. Ground truth is production telemetry (~/.trimtok/usage.jsonl plus the rotated .1). Run `scripts/audit_usage.py` for the honest split, per-gate buckets, size percentiles, mechanism breakdown and retrieve analysis — do not hand-roll a fresh one-off script each session, and do not trust a claimed number you did not recompute.
- Retrieval dependency: every compressed output that emits a #ref relies on CCR retrievability. If retrieval fails (TTL expiry, process restart, DB corruption), intelligence is permanently lost. Treat retrieval as a correctness requirement, not an optimization.
- Do not pre-empt the full compression pipeline with early-skip heuristics on text kind — the noise-drop (windowing) still reduces size even when there are no folds. The reverted_gate cascade (nano header → lossless strip → revert) already handles non-compressible payloads correctly. Pre-empting it bypasses the noise-drop and produces identical-or-worse output. Let the pipeline run and revert naturally.
- Fuzzy fold via rapidfuzz is implemented in `_fold_repeats` (similarity ≥ 0.85, digit normalization, length guard < 200 chars, adjacent-only). Do not extend to `_fold_templates` (Drain) without real-telemetry verification — Drain relies on exact tokenization.
## Reporting an audit
Lead with the honest number and the inflated one side by side, then a table of buckets by token weight (gate, before tokens, % of all tokens, saved %), then levers ranked by tokens-at-stake per unit of effort. State which claims are measured, which are inferred from a code read, and which are still hypotheses ("skeleton never fires in production could be the size threshold OR the targeted-slice rule") — never dress a code-read inference as a trace. Name explicitly what you did not read or did not verify at the end. This user wants the unflattering number first and the disagreement stated on technical grounds, not a summary that makes the tool look good.

## Known pitfalls
See references/known-pitfalls.md for distilled findings (polarity, slot collapse, hash collision, WAL bloat, cross-process alias, detect_kind misclassify, tiktoken fallback, fuzzy fold).
